title: CRLR/263/2022 of NISHI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.263 of 2022
Smt. Nishi and another ...Revisionists
Versus

State of Uttarakhand and another ...Respondents
Present:-
Mr. Nikhil Singhal, Advocate for the revisionists.
Mr. Pankaj Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Instant revision is preferred against the impugned
order dated 08.03.2022, passed in Suit No.79 of 2020, Smt.
Nishi and Another Vs. Sandeep Manwani, by the court of
Judge, Family Court, Haridwar. By it, an application for
interim maintenance filed by the revisionists, under Section
125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, was allowed
and the private respondent was directed to pay Rs.2000/-
per month interim maintenance to the revisionist no.1, his
wife and Rs.1,000/- per month interim maintenance to the
respondent no.2, his son.
2. Heard learned counsel for the revisionists and
perused the record.
3. Notice was issued to the private respondent
which was served on him as reported by the Registry, but he
does not put his appearance.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionists would submit
that the gross salary of the private respondent is

2
Rs.15,262.9 /- per month in the month of October, 2021. In
view, thereof, the amount of interim maintenance which has
been awarded to the revisionists is much inadequate.
5. In fact, the affidavit filed by the private
respondent, pursuant to the judgment in the case of
Rajnesh Vs. Neha and Another, (2021) 2 SCC 324, has also
been filed, in which the private respondent categorically
disclosed his salary as Rs. 9,309/-, per month with
Rs.5,953/- as petrol expenses. If added together, it comes to
Rs.15,262/-. Does it mean that in the month of October,
2021, the private respondent received total Rs.15,262/-,
including Rs.9,309/- salary and Rs.5,953/- as petrol
expenses.
6. Reference has been made to another document
regarding salary of private respondent for the month of
October, 2021, in which the earning for the month has been
recorded as Rs. 9309.31/-. It is argued that Rs.15,262/- is
per month salary of the private respondent, excluding
petrol.
7. This Court cannot take the salary of the private
respondent as Rs. 15,262/- per month. In his affidavit, the
private respondent has categorically stated that he gets
Rs.9309/- salary and for a particular month, he disclosed
that he received Rs. 5,953/- as petrol expenses. Total of
which makes out to Rs.15,262/-

3
8. Undoubtedly, Rs. 3,000/- total maintenance is a
very meagre amount. But then, it is always comparative to
the income of the spouse. It is always very tough to reach at
the exact amount of maintenance that is required for a
person. The Court makes estimation based on the attending
circumstances. According to the private respondent, he is a
delivery boy with Zomato. It is told that the revisionist no.1
is staying with her father. The amount of maintenance that
has been awarded is interim maintenance amount. Parties
have yet to adduce evidence.
9. Having considered the resources of the private
respondent, this Court is of the view that the amount of
maintenance does not warrant any interference.
10. Learned counsel for the revisionists would submit
that directions may be issued to the court below to expedite
the trial of the case. Undoubtedly, such matters need
expeditious disposal, after all it is a remedy to meet the day-to-day expenses of a person. With these observations, the
revision deserves to be dismissed at the stage of admission
itself.
11. The revision is dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 14.12.2022
Jitendra
